body:
§46.4 stores lastSyncedAt and consecutiveFailures on the channel record precisely so a person
can tell a quiet peer from a failing one — and no person-shaped surface shows either. Today the
only reader is `loam federate list` in a shell on the store's own machine. The admin page shows
the channel's pool as a bare container row, so a peer that has been unreachable since Monday
reads as "quiet" — the exact H9 shape the fields were stored to defeat. Worse: the admin page is
already federation's sever-confirm surface (an MCP-staged drop completes there, §46.5), so a
person today confirms an irreversible purge on a page that cannot show whether the channel was
healthy.

Build: render channel health on /admin, read from the same channel-record deltas
`channelStatusImpl` / `readChannels` already resolve (src/federation/channel.ts). For each
channel whose pool lives in the signed-in user's subtree, show: channel name, prefix,
receiving/blessing state, lastSyncedAt, consecutiveFailures. A channel with
consecutiveFailures > 0 renders visually distinct. The container-drop confirm page for a channel
pool includes the same health line above the confirm button. This is repair — visibility of
data designed for humans — not new law; no new route wider than the page's existing
subtree contract.

Two things the builder needs on day one:
- Fixture prerequisite: openChannelImpl declares a missing `into` container with NO parent
  edge, so a bare openChannel puts the pool outside every user's subtree and nothing renders.
  The test first declares the receiving container as a child inside the signed-in user's
  subtree (parent edge — admin-containers.test.ts is the precedent), THEN opens the channel
  into it.
- Render convention: lastSyncedAt === 0 means NEVER SYNCED and must render as words, never as
  a zero timestamp — mirror the loam_federate_status handler (src/server/http.ts), which
  already encodes this H9 convention.

Acceptance criteria — each verified by a server test driving the real page with the shared
session fixture (test/helpers/session-fixture.ts; do not write a sixteenth copy):
(a) /admin shows, for a channel in the user's subtree, its lastSyncedAt and consecutiveFailures,
    server-rendered. Verify: new test test/server/admin-channel-health.test.ts.
(b) A channel with consecutiveFailures > 0 carries a distinguishing marker in the markup; a
    healthy channel does not (two-sided). Verify: same test file.
(c) The drop-confirm page for a channel pool includes the channel's health line. Verify: same
    test file.
(d) Subtree contract preserved: a second user whose subtree holds no channels sees no health
    rows (two-sided against leakage). Verify: same test file, two-user fixture.

Merge tier: repair — self-merges on green + clean P5 + clean audit.
title: Channel health on /admin — the sever-confirm page can see what it severs
